items.description: Corinto is the main Pacific seaport of Nicaragua, handling a significant portion of the country's imports and exports.
Hacienda San Jacinto is a historic site where a decisive battle occurred in 1856 during the National War.
Iglesia La Merced in Granada is a colonial-era church noted for its ornate Baroque facade and historical resilience.
Fortaleza La Polvora is a colonial-era fortification in Granada built to protect the city's gunpowder stores.
Selva Negra is an eco-resort and coffee plantation located in the lush highlands of Matagalpa.
Heriberto Sanchez Amusement Park offers a variety of recreational facilities for families in the region.
Granada's Central Park is a vibrant hub of daily life, surrounded by colonial buildings and local vendors.
Finca El Platanal is a sustainable farm dedicated to the traditional production of high-quality cacao.
Finca Ecologica La Bomba is an educational coffee farm focused on environmentally friendly cultivation techniques.
Solentiname Archipelago is a group of islands in Lake Nicaragua renowned for its community of artists and rich birdlife.
Tisey-Estanzuela Natural Reserve is a mountainous protected area near Esteli, offering hiking trails and waterfalls.
Zapatera Island is a volcanic island in Lake Nicaragua, protected for its unique flora and historical archaeological sites.
The San Lorenzo Cloud Forest is a cool, misty habitat home to a variety of bird species and lush vegetation.
Estero Real is a major wetland area and estuary in the Gulf of Fonseca, vital for marine biodiversity.
Cerro El Arenal is a natural reserve in the northern highlands, providing important forest cover and habitat.
Rio Wawa is a significant river in the North Caribbean region, flowing through dense tropical landscapes.
The Meseta de los Pueblos is a fertile plateau region, known for its pleasant climate and agricultural productivity.
Selva de las Nubes is a mountainous forest area characterized by high altitude and consistent cloud cover.
Valle de Osua is a scenic valley area known for its geological features and rural landscapes.
The Meseta de Jinotega is a high, mountainous plateau essential for coffee and diverse vegetable farming.
Cerro La Quinta is a prominent mountain formation offering views over the surrounding northern landscape.
